title: sum

atoms.evidence: if (not keepdim) and (dim is not None): grad_out = np.expand_dims(grad_out, dim); return np.broadcast_to(grad_out, x.shape) — the canonical 2-step expand_dims + broadcast_to inverse-of-sum

Markdown: 'broadcast operation effectively copies our tensor, giving it more gradient paths that we need to sum over. Similarly, the backwards operation for summing is broadcasting' — explicit duality statement

6 lambda registrations in one cell: BACK_FUNCS.add_back_func(np.add, 0, lambda...: unbroadcast(grad_out, x)); ... add_back_func(np.true_divide, 1, lambda...: unbroadcast(grad_out * (-x / y**2), y)) — the bulk-register-lambdas idiom
new_grad_out = np.full_like(x, 0); np.add.at(new_grad_out, coerce_index(index), grad_out) — scatter via np.add.at to handle repeated indices
argmax = wrap_forward_fn(_argmax, is_differentiable=False); test cell asserts not b.requires_grad and b.recipe is None
wrap_forward_fn(_argmax, is_differentiable=False) — explicit use of the flag

Whole markdown section 'In-Place Operations' demonstrates safe_example()/unsafe_example() with add_/sub_; explains 'RuntimeError: a leaf Variable that requires grad is being used in an in-place operation'

Markdown section 'Mixed Scalar-Tensor Operations' explains why Tensor needs both __mul__ and __rmul__: 'Without __rmul__ defined, executing 2 * a when a is a Tensor would try to call 2.__mul__(a)'; test asserts 2 * b backprops correctly
sum/add/subtract/true_divide/getitem/argmax all wrapped + registered in this notebook

_sum(x, dim=None, keepdim=False) — dim and keepdim must flow through Recipe.kwargs to sum_back; tests.test_sum_keepdim_false specifically tests this plumbing
All registered backwards (sum_back, add/sub/div lambdas, getitem_back) use the (grad_out, out, x, ...) shape
All 6 lambdas for add/sub/div use unbroadcast(grad_out, x_or_y) — the broadcasting concern from R9.1 fired throughout
Every add/sub/div lambda wraps with unbroadcast(...) — the 3.1 pattern applied 6 times in this single cell
